title: Neural networks distinguished experimental pain subtypes from mouse serum fingerprints
summary: The study reports that serum MALDI-TOF mass-spectral fingerprints combined with pain-response measures discriminated four experimental neuropathic and nociplastic pain models and their origins in mice. It presents a preclinical classification result, without identifying individual protein biomarkers; it does not establish human diagnosis.
ai_technology: Feed-forward artificial neural networks trained by back-propagation

evidence.tested: Internal leave-one-out validation on mouse-model samples; no independent external cohort or human clinical validation was reported.
evidence.unknown: No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.
evidence.ai_role: ANNs classified mouse pain subtypes from serum mass-spectral fingerprints, combined with selected functional pain measures.
